item.title: Elder Tissa: Abandoning a hundred bowls of gold and precious metal, I take an ordinary clay bowl. This is the second time I have been…
item.description:
Elder Tissa:

Abandoning a hundred bowls of gold and precious metal,
I take an ordinary clay bowl.
This is the second time I have been consecrated.

From: Theragāthā 1.97

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of teaching proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, one following the other. What two? 'See evil…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of teaching proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, one following the other. What two? 'See evil as evil' — this is the first teaching. Having seen evil as evil, 'Be disenchanted, abandon it, be liberated from it' — this is the second teaching. Bhikkhus, these are the two kinds of teaching proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, one following the other.

By the Tathāgata, the Buddha,
Compassionate to all beings,
Two teachings are expounded
Step by step, Dhamma after Dhamma,
One following the other.

First, see evil as evil,
Then, being dispassionate toward it,
Abandon it completely.
From that, with mind dispassionate,
Make an end of suffering.

From: Itivuttaka 39

item.title: Kassapa, if a bhikkhu dwells cultivating a mind of compassion, without hatred, without malice, and with the destruction of the taints, he personally realizes and…
item.description:
Kassapa, if a bhikkhu dwells cultivating a mind of compassion, without hatred, without malice, and with the destruction of the taints, he personally realizes and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in this very life. That bhikkhu, Kassapa, is called a samaṇa, is called a brahmin.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 8 – Mahāsīhanādasutta

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, whatever streams flow into the great ocean and whatever rain falls from the sky, the great ocean does not thereby appear to…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, whatever streams flow into the great ocean and whatever rain falls from the sky, the great ocean does not thereby appear to decrease or increase. So too, bhikkhus, even if many bhikkhus attain final Nibbāna without remainder, Nibbāna does not thereby appear to decrease or increase. This, bhikkhus, is the fifth wonderful, marvelous quality in this Dhamma and Discipline. Seeing this, seeing this, bhikkhus delight in this Dhamma and Discipline.

From: Udāna 5.5

item.title: Elder Sambhūta: One who, when he should go slowly, goes quickly, One who, when he should go quickly, goes slowly — That fool, lacking right…
item.description:
Elder Sambhūta:

One who, when he should go slowly, goes quickly,
One who, when he should go quickly, goes slowly —
That fool, lacking right method, goes to suffering.

His benefit diminishes like the moon in the dark fortnight.
He meets disgrace and opposes his friends.

One who, when he should go slowly, goes slowly,
One who, when he should go quickly, goes quickly —
That wise one, with right method, goes to happiness.

His benefit is fulfilled like the moon in the bright fortnight.
He gains fame and honor, not opposing his friends.

From: Theragāthā 4.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, a person himself possesses faith and also encourages others to have faith; himself possesses moral shame and encourages others to have moral shame;…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, a person himself possesses faith and also encourages others to have faith; himself possesses moral shame and encourages others to have moral shame; himself possesses moral dread and encourages others to have moral dread; himself is learned and encourages others to be learned; himself is energetic and encourages others to be energetic; himself is mindful and encourages others to be mindful; himself possesses wisdom and encourages others to possess wisdom. Such a person, bhikkhus, is called a genuine person even more than a genuine person.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.202

item.title: Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor…
item.description:
Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is no sloth and torpor in me.' And he understands how unarisen sloth and torpor arises; and he understands how arisen sloth and torpor is abandoned; and he understands how abandoned sloth and torpor will not arise in the future.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 22 – Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta

item.title: Elder Nun Upacālā: Mindful, with the Dhamma-eye, A bhikkhunī training the faculties, Penetrates the peaceful path, Practiced by the supreme person. Why do you not…
item.description:
Elder Nun Upacālā:

Mindful, with the Dhamma-eye,
A bhikkhunī training the faculties,
Penetrates the peaceful path,
Practiced by the supreme person.

Why do you not like birth?
One born enjoys sensual pleasures.
Enjoy sensual pleasures,
Do not regret it later.

One who is born is subject to death,
Hands and feet are cut off,
Killed, bound, afflicted.
Afterwards, suffering comes.

Born in the Sakya clan,
The Buddha, the undefeated one,
Taught me the Dhamma,
To overcome birth.

He taught the Noble Eightfold Path,
About suffering, the origin of suffering,
About overcoming suffering,
And the path to the end of suffering.

Having heard his words,
I live delighting in the teaching.
I have attained the three knowledges,
Done is the Buddha's teaching.

Everywhere, joy is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know thus, Evil One!
You are defeated, O Death.

From: Therīgāthā 7.3

item.title: Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said:…
item.description:
Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said: 'Venerable Sir, this entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good association.' - 'Good, good, Sāriputta! This entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good association. Sāriputta, for a bhikkhu with good friends, good companions, good associates, it can be expected that the Noble Eightfold Path will be developed, that the Noble Eightfold Path will be cultivated.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 45.3

item.title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as reason, with sensual desire itself as cause, they engage…
item.description:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as reason, with sensual desire itself as cause, they engage in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. Having engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, after death, with the breakup of the body, they are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, such is the danger of sensual desires, bringing suffering in the future, a mass of suffering, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as source, with sensual desire as reason.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
